t:
(a) None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to maintain or establish a computer network unless such network blocks the viewing, downloading, and exchanging of pornography. 
    (b) Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit the use of funds necessary for any Federal, State, tribal, or local law enforcement agency or any other entity carrying out criminal investigations, prosecution, or adjudication activities.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of State, tribal, or local law enforcement agencies signals outside-party involvement. But those entities appear only in an exception to a funding restriction on computer networks; there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision, so this is an appropriations limitation and not participation.
fable.s: Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit the use of funds necessary for any Federal, State, tribal, or local law enforcement agency or any other entity carrying out criminal investigations, prosecution, or adjudication activities.

opus.w: This section only limits how funds may be spent: computer networks paid for under the Act must block pornography. It adds an exception for law enforcement and prosecution work. State, tribal and local agencies are mentioned only as entities covered by that exception, not as parties the federal government must consult before deciding something. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue, so it is not participation.
opus.s: Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit the use of funds necessary for any Federal, State, tribal, or local law enforcement agency or any other entity carrying out criminal investigations, prosecution, or adjudication activities.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Subsection (b) names "State, tribal, or local law enforcement" agencies, which are outside the federal government, so the section might look like it involves outside parties. That reading fails because those entities only appear in an exception to a funding restriction. No outsider is consulted, holds a hearing, sits on an advisory body, comments on a rule or gets a right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section imposes a restriction on the use of federal funds for computer networks that do not block pornography. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The only entities mentioned are federal, state, tribal, or local law enforcement agencies, but the exemption for them is not a participatory process; it is a carve-out from the restriction. There is no mechanism for outside input described.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the law restricts how federal funds are used, it implicitly requires consultation with users or administrators to implement the blocking technology. However, the text itself contains no requirement for consultation, comment periods, hearings, or advisory committees involving outside parties. It is a direct mandate on the use of funds.
